_readme: THE GOLDEN-PATH LEG REGISTER — [pipeline N-6] Private/company/pipeline/06-app-build.md
N-6 names a SIX-LEG golden path — anonymous -> sign in -> purchase (sandbox) -> entitlement flips
-> feature unlocks -> account delete purges — and asks for exactly one integration E2E on web that
covers it, wired into a named workflow.
THE DEFECT THIS FILE EXISTS FOR. Measured 2026-07-29 and re-measured 2026-08-02: the only
implementation of that path in the tree, apps/subly/integration_test/app_test.dart, declares TWO
tests and proves TWO of the six legs. There is no purchase, no entitlement flip, no feature unlock
and no account delete in it. So a green, non-skipped, fresh nightly still does not mean what N-6
says it means — and until this register existed, nothing anywhere wrote that number down. A
criterion whose right-hand side is undefined cannot reject anything.
🔄 THREE OF SIX SINCE 2026-08-08. `account-delete-purges` moved to `asserted`: the suite now
declares THREE tests and the third walks the erasure end to end against the deployed API. The two
sentences above are left as written because they are a dated measurement, not a status line — the
count that is checked is the one assert-e2e-legs.mjs computes on every run, and a prose number
edited by hand is the second copy that drifts. The three legs still blocked are the money rail's,
and they share one live blocker.
🔴 THE RULE THAT MAKES THIS FILE MEAN ANYTHING: A LEG IS 'asserted' ONLY IF THE SUITE PROVES IT.
Every `asserted` leg carries `anchors` — expressions that must appear in the E2E's
COMMENT-STRIPPED source. tooling/ci/assert-e2e-legs.mjs resolves each one; a leg that claims to be
asserted and whose anchors no longer resolve fails the build. That is the equality N-6 asks for:
the number of legs the record claims equals the number the suite actually proves.
Comment-stripping is not a formality here. app_test.dart's own header narrates the six-night
outage and contains the string `tap('Skip')` inside a comment, so a raw-text scan would resolve
the onboarding anchor against the PROSE DESCRIBING THE BUG rather than against any test.
🔴 A BLOCKED LEG'S EXCUSE IS ITSELF CHECKED. Every `blocked` leg names a `blockedBy` that
assert-e2e-legs.mjs re-evaluates against the real tree on every run (the BLOCKERS_STILL_REAL
pattern from assert-screen-set.mjs). If the blocker has shipped, the build FAILS — so 'blocked by
the money rail' cannot outlive the money rail, and the day apps/subly starts selling something the
three legs below stop being excusable in the same run. Blocked legs also PRINT on every run; a gap
that is silent is a gap nobody closes.
⚠️ WEB ONLY, BY POLICY, AND DATED. The cut was taken 2026-07-29. Apple 3.1.1 and Play's billing
policy require IAP for digital goods, so a Paddle web checkout cannot be the unlock path on iOS or
Android AT ALL — the purchase->unlock leg is not merely unimplemented off web, it is structurally
invalid there, and the IAP rail is routed to [5]/[10]. The other four platforms' absence is a COST
choice and not a tooling limit: `flutter test integration_test/` is documented for Android, iOS,
Windows, macOS and Linux (Linux needs xvfb-run), and the cheapest widening is Linux desktop on the
ubuntu runner already paid for. MASTER_PLAN.md:163 (DoD §4-H) demands the integration E2E 'per
environment' — six. This keeps ONE. §4-H wins on intent, N-6 on cost, and the narrowing is
recorded here as an explicit dated cut rather than left as a silent overrule.
⚠️ The Apple/Play guideline numbers are carried from 00-STAGE-3-14-RESEARCH.md and were NOT re-read
from developer.apple.com in this environment. COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH, cited with the word attached.
⚠️ ONE APP, STATED. e2e.yml is Subly-hardcoded and the brick stamps no integration_test/ at all, so
app #2 is born with no E2E and no harness to put one in. Generalising e2e.yml to a per-app matrix
is [9]R-1; stamping the E2E scaffold into the template is [3]S-2. This register describes the one
E2E that exists, and says so rather than implying a matrix.

legs.asks: a stranger with no account reaches the app and can move through first-run
real credentials against live Supabase move the user off the login screen and into the app
a sandbox purchase completes from inside the app
the entitlement the purchase bought is read back and flips to active
a feature that was gated before the purchase is usable after it
deleting the account from inside the app really erases the user and its rows
_why: PROMOTED 2026-08-08, and the excuse it replaced is the THIRD this leg has killed — which is the
design working three times. v1 'apps/subly has no delete-account call site' died when [ADR 027]
shipped the control. v2 'no deployed route erases apps/subly own database' died when
services/subly-api shipped DELETE /v1/account and the shared route began relaying to it. v3 'no
e2e step exercises the erasure route against the deployed API' dies here, because there is now a
step: integration_test/app_test.dart's third test signs in as a SECOND throwaway user, writes a
subscription through the live Worker, deletes the account from inside the running app, and lands
on the login screen — and tooling/e2e/verify_purged.mjs then re-reads live D1 and the GoTrue
🔴 THE ANCHORS BELOW COVER THE CLIENT HALF ONLY, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. They
resolve in the suite, which is all this guard can read. A client can only report what it was
told, so 'the app said Account deleted' is not 'the rows are gone' — the server-side half is
tooling/e2e/verify_purged.mjs, wired into e2e.yml between the D1 read-back and the teardown, and
it is held in place by assert-e2e-proof-fresh.mjs's REQUIRED_WORK rather than by this file.
Splitting the proof is deliberate; claiming the whole leg from four string matches would be the
⚠️ A SECOND THROWAWAY USER IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT TIDINESS. The delete walk destroys the account it
signs in with, and verify_row.mjs asserts COUNT(*) >= 1 for the FIRST user after the drive. One
user would mean leg 6 could only pass by turning leg 2 red.
